doc.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: Joining Dizzy Gillespie's band
summary: He joined Dizzy's band with Lee Morgan, Benny Golson and Melba Liston, mostly learning, and wrote later for the United Nations band.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: You’ve played an awful big role in Dizzy Gillespie’s career.
Well I think you had a good positive effect on what he was able to do. Would you agree with that?

Well I’ll tell you, we have to look at that. Because I joined Dizzy’s band in either the late fifties or the early sixties. And the band that I joined was the band with Lee Morgan, Benny Golson, Wynton Kelly, Melba Liston was the musical director, and they were playing so much music man, my head was just — they had my head spinning. I never wrote anything for the band. Because the music that they were playing, the arrangements were so good that I just didn’t feel like I wanted to try to write something coming up to that level of arranging that they were doing. So actually I was just learning. I wasn’t able to contribute much or anything. They had all the great soloists there, they had the great arrangers there and everything. Dizzy was even writing himself, and Dizzy was playing fantastic himself. His chops were strong. And they were playing all these great arrangements. So I didn’t contribute that much to him until later when I joined the United Nations band. I started doing some writing for that. But it was always still very intimidating to be writing for him, because he was such a great arranger himself. Standards were very high.
